item.text:
Turn complete. Report updated at [report.md](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-09_14-01-25-hashicorp_raft-baseline/work/report.md).

This turn I closed the last obvious coverage gap with a third independent harness targeting the version-gated code paths.

`work/zz_audit_mixedproto_test.go` (gated behind `-tags auditdiag`) builds a protocol-2 cluster of three nodes, grows it with a protocol-3 node via the ID-based `AddVoter`, then runs continuous writes across three leader-isolation partitions — repeatedly exercising the `prepareLog`'s `protocolVersion > 2` config handling and the `LogConfiguration` vs deprecated-config-format paths that Finding 1's trigger sits next to.

```
go test -tags auditdiag -v -count=5 -run '^TestAuditMixedProtocolInvariants$' .
--- PASS ×5   ok  github.com/hashicorp/raft
# e.g. nodes=4 acked=814 node0_applied=815 missing=0
```

All four nodes converged to an identical applied sequence with `missing=0` in every run: no divergence and no acked-command loss across the mixed-version cluster under partition. Clean negative for the mixed-version config path.

I also checked the disposable runtime GOPATH for a second copy of the module that might serve as a pristine reference — there is none (only my own extracted zip), so the byte-diff route stays blocked offline.

Running total from the three harnesses is now roughly 16,000 acked commands with zero lost and zero divergence:

- randomized leader isolation: 10 runs / 40 rounds / ~7k cmds
- snapshot catch-up under partition (forced `InstallSnapshot`): 5 runs / ~5k cmds
- mixed protocol-2/3 under partition: 5 runs / ~4k cmds

Hygiene confirmed: `go vet .` is clean with no tags, so the five `zz_audit_*` diagnostic files stay out of the captured suite's default build and only run with `-tags auditdiag`.

The audit's conclusions are unchanged: one confirmed low-severity defect (Finding 1 — `testing.go`'s `EnsureSamePeers` freezes its reference peer set, making `TestRaft_ProtocolVersion_Upgrade_2_3` fail ~15–30% on a healthy cluster), no consensus-level defect found by source review or by four independent methods, and the single honest open question of whether Finding 1 is the injected mutation or a latent upstream flake — unanswerable offline because the module cache's provenance can't be trusted.
